response.generated_text:
### G1-2 – Management of relationships with suppliers

Pennon recognises strong supplier relationships as an important component of its business model. We work closely with suppliers, monitor their performance against our expectations and require them to uphold our standards, align with relevant policies, protect human rights and promote good working conditions. Our Code of Conduct applies to permanent and temporary employees, and we expect suppliers and contractors to comply with equivalent legal and ethical guidance. Supplier codes of conduct support this approach by requiring people to be treated fairly and with respect and dignity.

Procurement processes incorporate economic, financial, environmental and social considerations. Sustainable procurement policies apply whole-life costing and defined environmental and social responsibility criteria to goods and services, supporting long-term value for Pennon and its customers. South West Water sources purchases through competitive markets and operates strict procurement policies requiring suppliers to follow clearly defined sustainability and ethical working-practice standards. Its mixed-economy supply-chain model combines smaller specialist businesses with larger strategic partners. The procurement strategy also supports proactive relationship management with key and strategic suppliers representing the large majority of expenditure.

Supplier selection and contract management form part of Pennon’s risk-management arrangements. Rigorous assessment criteria are applied to suppliers, including due diligence relating to suppliers, technologies and acquisitions. For significant capital projects, skilled project-management resources and oversight boards provide additional control. Contractual protections may include back-to-back agreements, supplier guarantees and penalty clauses. Performance on major contracts is reported regularly and post-project appraisals are undertaken. These measures address the risk of contractor or supplier failure, including delays, increased costs and potential legal action.

Governance of supply-chain matters is integrated into Pennon’s wider sustainability, risk and internal-control framework. The Sustainability Committee has reviewed sustainable procurement and practices within the supply chain, together with the coverage and appropriateness of Group policies and performance against sustainability targets. Procurement practices have also been within the scope of internal audit reporting reviewed by the Audit Committee. The Group-wide compliance and ethics programme and Code of Conduct further support consistent expectations across business operations and supplier relationships.

In 2019, Pennon’s average time to pay invoices was **30 days**, measured from the date on which the relevant contractual or statutory payment term began. This represented an improvement from **58 days in 2018**. Timely payment supports constructive and stable supplier relationships, including within a supply chain that incorporates smaller specialist companies. Pennon continued to manage supplier relationships through clear standards, competitive procurement, performance oversight and risk-based contractual controls.

### G1-2 – Management of relationships with suppliers

Pennon recognises strong supplier relationships as an important component of its business model. We work closely with suppliers, monitor their performance against our expectations and require them to uphold our standards, align with relevant policies, protect human rights and promote good working conditions. Our Code of Conduct applies to permanent and temporary employees, and we expect suppliers and contractors to comply with equivalent legal and ethical guidance. Supplier codes of conduct support this approach by requiring people to be treated fairly and with respect and dignity.

Procurement processes incorporate economic, financial, environmental and social considerations. Sustainable procurement policies apply whole-life costing and defined environmental and social responsibility criteria to goods and services, supporting long-term value for Pennon and its customers. South West Water sources purchases through competitive markets and operates strict procurement policies requiring suppliers to follow clearly defined sustainability and ethical working-practice standards. Its mixed-economy supply-chain model combines smaller specialist businesses with larger strategic partners. The procurement strategy also supports proactive relationship management with key and strategic suppliers representing the large majority of expenditure.

Supplier selection and contract management form part of Pennon’s risk-management arrangements. Rigorous assessment criteria are applied to suppliers, including due diligence relating to suppliers, technologies and acquisitions. For significant capital projects, skilled project-management resources and oversight boards provide additional control. Contractual protections may include back-to-back agreements, supplier guarantees and penalty clauses. Performance on major contracts is reported regularly and post-project appraisals are undertaken. These measures address the risk of contractor or supplier failure, including delays, increased costs and potential legal action.

Governance of supply-chain matters is integrated into Pennon’s wider sustainability, risk and internal-control framework. The Sustainability Committee has reviewed sustainable procurement and practices within the supply chain, together with the coverage and appropriateness of Group policies and performance against sustainability targets. Procurement practices have also been within the scope of internal audit reporting reviewed by the Audit Committee. The Group-wide compliance and ethics programme and Code of Conduct further support consistent expectations across business operations and supplier relationships.

In 2019, Pennon’s average time to pay invoices was **30 days**, measured from the date on which the relevant contractual or statutory payment term began. This represented an improvement from **58 days in 2018**. Timely payment supports constructive and stable supplier relationships, including within a supply chain that incorporates smaller specialist companies. Pennon continued to manage supplier relationships through clear standards, competitive procurement, performance oversight and risk-based contractual controls.
